newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZAGALLO CAMPAIGNS FOR ARTISTIC GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZAGALLO CAMPAIGNS FOR ARTISTIC GAME.

text.p: Brazil want to win the next World Cup in the best traditions of their skilled, attacking game and hope to take another step in that direction when they meet Italy in a repeat of the 1994 final on Sunday.
"I want a World Cup with art," coach Mario Zagallo said looking ahead to Brazil's defence of their title in France next year.
"Strength at the service of technique and not technique to support strength," he added as Brazil prepared for the Tournoi de France match against the Italians.

"I don't want others to think: 'I'm not going to let them play'. I want to play in the traditional Brazilian way. I want to go back to the past," said the 65-year-old Zagallo, a World Cup winner as both player and coach.
Zagallo does not think of the game against Cesare Maldini's Italians as a rematch of the World Cup final which Brazil won on penalties. He said a revenge match was possible only in a World Cup.

He believes the Italians have come to France for this World Cup dress rehearsal in better shape than Brazil, despite his side's wonderful 1-1 draw with the hosts on Tuesday and Italy's 2-0 loss to England on Wednesday.
"They are at a better stage because of the World Cup qualifiers," said Zagallo, glad to get competitive games for his side who, as holders, do not have to qualify for next year's finals.
After their three Tournoi matches, Brazil go to Bolivia for the Copa America, the South America championship they have won four times.
Zagallo has decided to put out an unchanged side against Italy from that which drew with France.
Maldini, contrary to what Zagallo said, considers his team ill-prepared for the tournament which falls at the wrong time of the season and in between World Cup qualifiers.
"My team has several physical problems," said Maldini, naming defender Ciro Ferrara and midfielders Roberto Di Matteo and Demetrio Albertini.
"We made many mistakes which we paid for dearly," he said after Wednesday's defeat. "We're below what we can do and the English were more tuned up."
The Italians beat England 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier at Wembley in February and face them again in Rome in October.
"Now we're going to play against Brazil who looked very strong to me," said Maldini, whose son and captain Paolo is one of the few survivors of the 1994 World Cup squad.
The younger Maldini, another player nursing an injury, missed Wednesday's match but could be fit to lead Italy against Brazil on Sunday.
Juventus goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi said the Italians were tired after a long, exhausting season.
"Some (players) have played 50 or 60 matches and are exhausted. We're not advancing any more...I hope we recover against Brazil," he said.
Maldini has doubts concerning his line-up for Sunday with Ferrara and Di Matteo suffering from leg injuries and Albertini from a back problem.
